answer: A sequential delay protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to evaluate non-parallelizable cryptographic proofs signed via falcon keys. At the dawn of every epoch, an agent must compute serial modular squarings to broadcast a verified state delta. An attacker must dedicate scarce, high-frequency processor cores per identity, making bulk creation cost-prohibitive. However, this perpetually burns electricity and remains vulnerable to adversaries using custom ASIC hardware.
